calls.title: Diane Hagglund and Ashley Stirrup
calls.summary: The meeting addressed several crucial elements for effective survey design and execution, emphasizing the need for a minimum of 300 participants, with 400 preferred for statistical confidence. Diane Hagglund highlighted that smaller sample sizes lead to a loss of credibility, while quality questions can mitigate this issue. Discussions also pointed towards the importance of targeting the right audience segments, integrating cost control with insightful analysis. The meeting noted that survey costs are primarily driven by participant sourcing and highlighted the need for clear, manageable question design focused on reducing bias. Additionally, the research's role as a central asset within a broader campaign to amplify reach through various content formats was stressed, underscoring the value of storytelling and strategic outreach.
calls.keywords: Participants, Survey Design, Cost Structure, PR Strategy, Audience Targeting, Campaign Planning

calls.title: Diane Hagglund and Ashley Stirrup
calls.summary: The discussion emphasizes AI coding's transformative role in product development, highlighting Growth Book's feature flagging and experimentation tools that facilitate gradual feature rollouts and A/B testing while ensuring safety. Diane Hagglund underscores challenges related to rapid feature changes that frustrate users and suggests customizable feature flags to enhance user experience. The need for experimentation is further stressed, particularly due to the unpredictable nature of AI outcomes. The meeting also defines target audiences for Growth Book, focusing on engineers and product managers in high-traffic B2C sectors. Additionally, a robust research methodology is proposed to explore attitudes toward experimentation, balancing qualitative insights with quantitative data, while next steps include drafting a proposal for further research alignment.
calls.keywords: AI coding, feature flags, A/B testing, product development, experimentation maturity, research report
